background.source: Cellular structure refers to the organization of components that make up living cells. These components include the ribosome, golgi apparatus, mitochondria, nucleus, and cell membrane. The nucleus is the control center of the cell and contains the genetic material, while the mitochondria are responsible for energy production. The golgi apparatus is involved in processing and packaging proteins, and the ribosomes are responsible for protein synthesis. The cell membrane acts as a barrier and regulates the movement of substances in and out of the cell. Understanding the cellular structure is crucial to understanding how cells function and interact with their environment.
background.target: A city is a human settlement of notable size with administratively defined boundaries that offers a multitude of services and facilities for its inhabitants. These include housing, transportation, sanitation, utilities, production of goods, communication and government representation. With more than half of the world’s population residing in cities, they have become significant players in global issues such as sustainable development and climate change. Sustainable cities, with a smaller ecological footprint per inhabitant, offer potential in fighting climate change but can have negative consequences such as concentrated pollution and urban heat islands. Capitals and religious sites also hold cultural significance within a nation or religion. These cities are often protected by city walls, which were historically built to prevent sieges and attacks. Overall, cities are important centres that influence the world around them and require planning and investment to ensure their sustainable development.
